summary: Frontend-only verification of the AnimatedTurtle speed() fix on /turtle/teach (TurtleTeaching page, which mounts <AnimatedTurtle code={code}/>). All 4 timing-sensitive tests from the review request passed. The bug (t.speed(0) crawling and the case 'speed' handler being a no-op) is fixed: speedRef mirrors state, speed=0 -> 0ms delay (instant), speed=1..10 -> (11-clamped)*50ms, and mid-run t.speed() changes propagate immediately via speedRef.current update inside the executeCommand's case 'speed' handler.

detailed_flow_results.route_used: /turtle/teach (TurtleTeaching) - Monaco editor value set via window.monaco.editor.getModels()[0].setValue(...), then native click on button:has(svg.lucide-play). Completion detected by waiting for the pause icon (svg.lucide-pause) to disappear.

T1_speed0_20steps.code: t.speed(0); for i in range(20): t.forward(50); t.left(18)
T1_speed0_20steps.notes: Would have taken ~30s (61 * 500ms) under the OLD buggy formula. Now near-instant, confirming speed=0 -> 0ms delay.

T2_speed1_4steps.code: t.speed(1); for i in range(4): t.forward(50); t.left(90) (draws a square)
T2_speed1_4steps.notes: speed(1) is now the SLOWEST animation (10*500=~5s max minus non-animated ops). Confirms speed(1) != speed(0).

T3_default_speed_20steps.code: for i in range(20): t.forward(30); t.left(18) (no t.speed() call)
T3_default_speed_20steps.notes: Confirms default speed=5 unchanged by fix ((11-5)*50=300ms per drawn step).

T4_midrun_speed_change.code: t.speed(1); t.forward(50); t.speed(0); for i in range(20): t.forward(30); t.left(18)
T4_midrun_speed_change.notes: CRITICAL - proves the speedRef change inside case 'speed' propagates mid-execution. If the ref weren't updated, this would be either ~20s (all slow) or ~0.5s (all instant) depending on capture timing.

T5_slider_regression.notes: The AnimatedTurtle toolbar visible on /turtle/teach shows only 4 buttons: Reset (lucide-rotate-ccw), Play/Pause, FastForward, Grid. There is NO on-screen speed slider in the toolbar for this component. The review request already flagged this as conditional ('if present'). Speed is exclusively controllable via t.speed() in code. The speed state variable exists and useEffect syncs speedRef -> speed, so if a slider is added later it will work.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is clean and minimal: speedRef added at line 976, new delay formula at line 1451-1461, case 'speed' handler updated at line 1613-1618, sync useEffect at line 2010-2014. All four hunks referenced in the review request are in place.

The useCallback deps for executeCommand correctly exclude `speed` (reads via ref), which is essential for mid-run t.speed() to work without re-memoizing the callback and restarting the animation loop.
AnimatedTurtle.jsx is 2410 lines — flagged in past iterations. Not related to this fix.

Consider adding data-testid attributes to the Play/Pause/Reset/FastForward buttons of AnimatedTurtle to make future timing-based tests less brittle (currently relies on svg.lucide-play / svg.lucide-pause classes).

No visible UI speed slider means users on /turtle/teach can ONLY change speed via t.speed() in code. If a UI slider is desired, the plumbing (speed state + speedRef sync useEffect) is already in place.
